video.hook: OpenAI just stretched prompt caching to 12 hours in the API. In Codex, if you're logged in, they say your cache never expires. That means you can come back to a long coding session hours later and not pay full price to reload all that context. I'm going to show you what that actually saves and where it doesn't help.

The Quiet OpenAI Update That Cuts Your API Bill
outline: What prompt caching is, in one minute: reusing a prompt prefix you already sent

Test: resume an old Codex session after a few hours and check whether it picks up fast
API side: how to structure prompts so the stable part gets cached

beats.line: OpenAI just made prompt caching last 12 hours.
Before, if you stepped away from a long session, the cache could expire and you'd pay to reload everything.
Now the API holds it for 12 hours, and logged-in Codex users keep it with no penalty for coming back later.
The trick: keep the stable stuff, like system prompts and docs, at the top so it gets reused.
Full breakdown and my resume test are on the channel.
